defs.def: a long period of time when there is little or no rain 久旱；旱灾

ex.s: “Basically, the provincial government is letting the insurance companies protect the Calgary-Edmonton urban area from hail,” Mr Stienwand says, “but they’re increasing drought risk as far east as Saskatchewan.”
ex.t: “基本上，省政府是在让保险公司保护卡尔加里-埃德蒙顿城区免受冰雹侵害，”斯坦万德先生说，“但他们正在向东远至萨斯喀彻温省增加干旱风险。”

ex.s: “We affect only a very small percentage of the total moisture in the air, so we cannot be causing drought,” Dr Krauss says.
ex.t: 克劳斯博士说："我们只影响空气中总湿度的极小一部分，因此不可能造成干旱。"

ex.s: We’ve also seen droughts and floods caused by these changes, which affect the water supply downstream.
ex.t: 我们还看到这些变化造成的干旱和洪水，影响了下游的供水。

ex.t: （图1）干旱 （图2）台风 （图3）暴风雪 （图4）海啸 （图5）野火 （图6）雪崩 （图7）地震 1.你认为哪一个最危险？

ex.s: Some trees make clicking noises when there is not enough water, indicating drought is arriving.
ex.t: 有些树木在没有足够的水时发出咔嗒声，表明干旱即将到来。

ex.s: This is likely to have led to a series of droughts, each lasting for a couple of years, including a “megadrought” around 900 AD.
ex.t: 这很可能导致了一系列干旱，每次持续数年，其中包括公元900年左右的一次"超级大旱"。

ex.s: Many scientists believe that these droughts were the main reason why Maya civilisation began to collapse at different rates in different places.
ex.t: 许多科学家认为，这些干旱是玛雅文明在不同地方开始以不同速度崩溃的主要原因。
